objectives: Hear /s/ followed immediately by /w/ at the beginning of taught words.
Blend /s/ and /w/ smoothly without inserting an extra vowel.
Distinguish the sw onset from /s/ alone and other taught blends.
Blend the onset with the remaining sounds and say the complete word.
concepts: Both consonants remain audible and in order.
No extra vowel belongs between onset consonants.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the start of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
Joining speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Hear /s/ then /w/, followed by the rest of the word.
Swim begins with sw; sit begins with /s/ alone.
Keep /s/ and /w/ in order, then blend the rest.

commonMistakes: Dropping /w/ and saying sim for swim.
Guessing before hearing the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Do not insert an extra vowel.
Blend the onset with the rest of the word.
revisionPoints: Swim and swan begin with sw.
Listen to the whole word before choosing.
